CMST 2034.title: Visual Media
CMST 2034.description: Planning and production of visual messages for delivery through print, photography, videography, websites, social media, and mobile applications. Theories and principles of visual communication important to individuals working in communication jobs. COURSE FEE $59. Pre: Sophomore standing

CMST 2064.title: The Tradition of Rhetoric and Societal Change
CMST 2064.description: Key theories and figures in rhetoric over the past 2,500 years. Evolution of rhetorical and critical perspectives in communication. Dynamic, critical nature of persuasive communication. Methodological approaches to rhetorical criticism, ethics of message creation, communication contexts, emerging perspectives, and impact of changing culture/society on rhetorical theory.

CMST 3044.title: Oral Communication Center Practicum
CMST 3044.description: Focus on peer pedagogy in a communication center to support development of oral communication competence among students across disciplines. Emphasis on oral communication theory applied to one-on-one support for students oral presentations. May repeat 1 time.

CMST 3064.title: Persuasion
CMST 3064.description: Theoretical foundations of persuasion; techniques of persuasion; contemporary persuasive practice and campaigns; persuasive media strategies. Junior standing required.

CMST 3124.title: Interpersonal Communication
CMST 3124.description: Basic theories and processes of person-to-person communication; interpersonal perception; verbal and nonverbal communication; establishment of relationships in the family and work situation. Junior standing required.

CMST 3134.title: Public Advocacy
CMST 3134.description: Practical reasoning and argumentation about questions of community significance, emphasizing critical thought, rhetorical strategies, and advocacy. Junior standing required.

CMST 3214.title: Professional Communication
CMST 3214.description: Theory and contemporary practice of professional oral communication, including interpersonal interaction, small group problem-solving, and public presentations. Emphasis on ethical exchanges in traditional or virtual workshops settings.

CMST 4174.title: Digital Advocacy Campaigns
CMST 4174.description: Study of advocacy campaigns with digital components. Rhetorical considerations in message construction, analysis of persuasive techniques, ethical standards, and strategies for campaign development. Senior standing required.

CMST 4214.title: Web Content Management Strategies
CMST 4214.description: Methodologies, tools, and strategies for managing workflow of communication projects for Web distribution. Software tools for Web-based communication. Quantitative and qualitative methods for usability and readability of Web content. Web analytics and content metrics to support decision making.

CMST 4244.title: Topics in Communication
CMST 4244.description: Selected topics in communication. Application of theory and research in selected context. Ethical and social dimensions of communication issues, policies, and effects. May be repeated with different content for a maximum of 6 credit hours. Pre: Junior standing.

CMST 4284.title: Communication for Training and Development
CMST 4284.description: Communication principles and practices for training and development. Communication roles, strategies, and products for learning in workplace environments.

CMST 4714.title: Senior Seminar in Communication
CMST 4714.description: In-depth study of an issue or theme in communication. Communication theories, issues, policies, effects, and contexts. Research and presentation of research. Pre: Senior standing.
CMST 4714.prereq: COMM 2024 and (CMST 2034 or ADV 2034 or JMC 2034)

CMST 5814.title: Seminar in Communication Studies
CMST 5814.description: Topical seminar examining various aspects of contemporary theory and research in interpersonal, public, and mediated human communication. Repeatable with different content for a maximum of six hours credit.
